A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how the mass and angular momentum per mass parameters of a Kerr metric and the radius of the orbit of a distant observer can be estimated from the red/blue shifts of photons emitted at certain points along a geodesic particle’s orbit around the black hole and their corresponding radii.

we are proposing a new relativistic method to estimate the mass and spin of a Kerr blackhole, as well as the radius of our orbital path around it, through a Bayesian statistical analysis of the observed red/blue shifts of photons emitted at certain points of our orbits.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a relativistic analysis of star orbits around a supermassive object in the Milky Way, like S2, S0-102 and S0-2, can be performed in a way that is fully consistent with the theory of General Relativity.

the red/blue shifts of photons emitted at the equatorial plane of geodesic particles moving around a Kerr black hole, as well as their orbital radii, provide a relativistic way of determining the mass and rotation of the hole, and the distance that separates it from the observer.

the red/blue shifts of photons emitted from stars and galactic gas and traveling along null geodesic trajectories towards a distant observer can be used to statistically estimate the parameters that characterize a Kerr black hole and the radius of a geodesic orbit of an observer.
